pub assume_specification<T, E, F, O: FnOnce(E) -> Result<T, F>>[
    Result::<T, E>::or_else
](result: Result<T, E>, op: O) -> (res: Result<T, F>)
    requires
        result is Err ==> op.requires((result->Err_0,)),
    ensures
        result is Ok ==> res == Result::<T, F>::Ok(result->Ok_0),
        result is Err ==> op.ensures((result->Err_0,), res),
;
ensures: result is Ok ==> res == Result::<T, F>::Ok(result->Ok_0)
candidates.rationale: The metadata resolves this alias method to Result::or_else. Its explicit branching and conditional FnOnce call are expressible using vstd closure contracts without inspecting lock state.
risks: The Err branch is only as precise as the closure's declared contract; lock poisoning and other hidden runtime effects remain unmodeled.

ensures: res == match result { Result::Ok(Option::Some(value)) => Option::Some(Result::Ok(value)), Result::Ok(Option::None) => Option::None, Result::Err(error) => Option::Some(Result::Err(error)), }
candidates.rationale: The source performs only a complete structural rearrangement of public Result and Option variants.
risks: The contract does not specify how a LockResult was produced or any invariant associated with a guard payload.
